newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks balanced operational budget - Lamassour.
newsitem.headline: France seeks balanced operational budget - Lamassour.

text.p: France's ruling coalition would aim to get the state's operational budget to break-even point by the year 2000, budget minister and government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said in an interview published on Monday.

He told business daily La Tribune that Finance Minister Jean Arthuis was planning to distinguish in the 1998 budget between state operational spending and state spending on investment and that rebalancing the former was a priority.
While it could still be possible to fund state investment spending through loans, this should not be the case for the operational spending side, he said.

"The deadline would be 2000. In 1997 the operational side registered a deficit of 115 billion francs, that shows the scale of effort needed if we are no longer to finance civil service pay and retirement through loans," he said.
Getting to breakeven would involve reducing the number of ministers by around half to 15 and reforming civil service staffing as well.

Lamassoure, whose centre-right government is in the throes of a parliamentary election campaign, said that reducing civil service staffing levels by non-replacement of retiring employees was not viable on a multi-annual basis and that a clear plan for the future would be needed.
